current_leader.name: Cloud support-plan right-sizing engine
current_leader.state_transition: monthly cloud spend and provider-independent operational/incident telemetry update -> recompute current support-tier cost and required SLA/features -> compare cheaper eligible tiers -> recommend KEEP/DOWNGRADE/UPGRADE at next permissible boundary -> verify support-fee delta
current_leader.why_survived: AWS, Google Cloud and Azure all expose recurring paid support plans with explicit monthly pricing/change boundaries, while current searches still did not find an exact continuous cross-cloud engine that combines support-tier economics with operational criticality/incident telemetry. The wedge remains read-only and the fee delta is deterministic.
strongest_evidence: AWS paid support has a one-month minimum and Business Support+/Enterprise/Unified Operations have explicit monthly minimum/percentage pricing; AWS allows Business Support+ downgrade from the console and Enterprise downgrade via TAM.
Google Cloud Standard, Enhanced and Premium Support have explicit minimum/percentage pricing, including $29/3%, $100/tiered, and $15,000/tiered structures.
Azure support plans are billed monthly and can be changed or cancelled in the Azure portal for eligible purchase channels.
AWS Support API requires a paid support plan, so a durable optimizer cannot depend on that API after recommending a downgrade to Basic.
current_leader.closest_threat: First-party support-plan calculators/change workflows plus partner-led support substitutes such as DoiT can absorb or economically neutralize part of the wedge. Broad FinOps/MSP platforms can also add support-plan review even though an exact continuous telemetry-aware optimizer was not found.
current_leader.smallest_intervention: Read cloud billing forecast, current support tier, workload criticality/SLOs, incident history and required response-time/features from provider-independent telemetry; output KEEP/DOWNGRADE/UPGRADE plus next-month fee delta and feature/risk tradeoff. No automatic plan change.
current_leader.monetization: Small per-accepted plan-change fee, low recurring monitoring fee, or capped share of verified support-fee savings over a defined measurement window.
current_leader.biggest_unresolved_risk: The correct support tier may be mostly static and driven by tail-risk insurance rather than historical ticket usage, so most value may collapse into an annual review; paid-plan-only support telemetry can also disappear after downgrade.
current_leader.next_research_test: Quantify real support-tier overprovisioning and change frequency using customer/FinOps evidence; search MSP/FinOps products for explicit support-plan optimization; test whether provider-independent incident/SLO telemetry predicts tier sufficiency well enough without paid Support APIs. Reject or demote if annual/static review captures most value or substitutes neutralize the economics.

runner_ups.note: Still clean but avoidable accelerated-settlement leakage remains unproven.
Programmable and measurable; incremental savings over competent static tuning remain unproven.

Apple's 15% reduced commission can create a large deterministic delta and proceeds are machine-readable, but enrollment is simple/first-party and requalification is mostly annual, weakening recurring monetization.
Strong structure but still lacks a sufficiently high-value defensible vertical.

demotions.reason: Support is tail-risk insurance; low case usage is not equivalent to waste. AWS Support API is paid-plan-only, so telemetry disappears after a downgrade to Basic unless provider-independent signals are used. Monetizable decision frequency remains unquantified.

new_candidates.state_transition: App Store proceeds/account relationships update -> eligibility for reduced 15% commission/requalification becomes true -> alert and prepare enrollment evidence -> verify commission-rate delta
new_candidates.fatal_or_open_issue: Apple makes enrollment straightforward and eligibility changes mostly annually, so this risks being a one-time checklist rather than a recurring tollbooth.

rejections.fatal_flaw: Exact first-party automation now exists: ShipStation Refund Assist automatically detects, voids and submits eligible unused USPS labels for refund; other shipping APIs expose direct void/refund primitives.
Multiple exact products now compare lease terms with CAM/operating-expense statements, produce clause-cited overcharge findings and recovery/dispute workflows.

new_search_rules: Do not infer support-tier waste from low support-ticket volume; support is partly tail-risk insurance and must be evaluated against workload criticality, SLOs and feature requirements.

If a cost-saving recommendation removes access to the telemetry API used to make that recommendation, the wedge must be redesigned around provider-independent signals or penalized for integration fragility.
A large percentage fee reduction with simple first-party enrollment can still fail the monetization gate when the state transition occurs only annually or collapses to a checklist.
